sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module overview and inputs
sections.what: Nothing runs here. It explains the valuation steps and the market inputs it expects.
sections.why: Gives the reader the method before the code.

sections.name: calculate_relevered_beta
sections.title: Adjusting beta for debt
sections.what: Raises the unlevered beta to account for the target debt level and the tax benefit of interest.
sections.why: Likely reason: debt makes shareholder risk higher, so the beta used for equity must include it.
sections.watch_out: It uses a target debt ratio, so the result depends on that chosen target rather than the actual debt level.

sections.name: calculate_cost_of_equity
sections.title: Required return for shareholders
sections.what: Works out the return shareholders should expect, using the risk-free rate, beta, and the equity and country risk premiums.
sections.why: Likely reason: it is the discount rate for equity.
sections.watch_out: Both premiums are multiplied by beta, so a high beta also magnifies country risk; check this is intended.

sections.name: calculate_wacc
sections.title: Blended cost of capital
sections.what: Blends the cost of equity and the after-tax cost of debt, weighted by the target debt-to-equity mix, to give one discount rate.
sections.why: Likely reason: the discounting needs a single rate that reflects both sources of funding.
sections.watch_out: The weights come from the debt-to-equity ratio, so a wrong ratio gives a wrong rate.

sections.name: discount_cash_flows
sections.title: Present value of each year's cash flow
sections.what: Discounts each year's cash flow back to today using the discount rate, compounding by year, with the first year left as it is.
sections.why: Money received in the future is worth less than money today.
sections.watch_out: The first cash flow is not discounted, so the list must begin at the current year or every value is overstated.

sections.name: calculate_terminal_value
sections.title: Value beyond the forecast period
sections.what: Estimates the value of all cash flows after the forecast using a growing perpetuity, then discounts that value back to today.
sections.why: Forecasts cannot run forever, so the terminal value captures the rest.
sections.watch_out: The terminal value is discounted by the full number of forecast years, which may be one year more than the timing of the last cash flow implies. The growth rate must also be below the discount rate.

sections.name: calculate_dcf_valuation (part 1)
sections.title: Running the full valuation steps
sections.what: Runs the steps in order: beta, cost of equity, cost of capital, present values, terminal value, and enterprise value, then subtracts net debt to get equity value.
sections.why: Gives callers a single entry point for a valuation.
sections.watch_out: Net debt is subtracted as given, so debt and cash must be in the same units as the cash flows.

sections.name: calculate_dcf_valuation (part 2)
sections.title: Returning the valuation components
sections.what: Returns all rates, cash flows, terminal value, and final values in one result, so each step can be traced.
sections.why: Lets the reader check every stage of the valuation.
sections.watch_out: Values are ordinary numbers and the result is not per share, so a per-share value needs a separate step.

summary: Estimates what the company is worth today by discounting its future free cash flows and a terminal value, using a cost of capital built from market inputs.
purpose: Produces the discount rates, present values, enterprise value, and equity value.
why: Discounting expected future cash is a standard way to value a business.
how: 1. Adjust beta for the target debt level. 2. Work out the cost of equity with the capital asset pricing model. 3. Blend the cost of equity and the after-tax cost of debt into one cost of capital. 4. Discount each year's free cash flow. 5. Value the years after the forecast with a terminal value and discount it. 6. Add these to get enterprise value, then subtract net debt to get equity value.
inputs: Free cash flow list; risk-free rate; equity risk premium; country risk premium; unlevered beta; pre-tax cost of debt; target debt-to-equity ratio; tax rate; terminal growth rate; net debt.
outputs: A dictionary with all rates and inputs, the cash flows and their present values, the terminal value, enterprise value, and equity value.
risks: The first cash flow is not discounted, so if it is a future year, the value is overstated. The terminal value is discounted by the number of forecast years, which may be one year more than the timing of the cash flows suggests. Nothing stops the terminal growth rate reaching or exceeding the cost of capital, which gives wrong results or an error. Results are ordinary numbers, not per-share values.
debug: Start by checking the cost of capital is in a sensible range. Check the terminal growth rate is below it. Confirm the first cash flow is the current year. Compare the sum of present values with the individual values.
